name: canopy-9a629f6b-blind28-ots
instr:
# Canopy: diagnosing a blockchain node gone wrong without a test suite

This source tree builds a node for a proof-of-stake chain: it keeps a copy of the ledger, agrees new blocks with other validators, accepts signed submissions from users, answers questions about what it has recorded, and keeps itself connected and current. Operating one built from this tree, an operator sees a long list of things come back wrong. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the callers changed; work that used to succeed now fails, and in one place it brings the process down.

Much of it shows up while a node is up and taking part in agreeing the next block. Applying a block that carries a single signed transfer against a freshly seeded chain no longer yields a new header and a result row: on a node started without a measurement sink wired up, the call dies partway through and the height never advances. A proposal whose block hash disagrees with the block the replica built for itself is now waved through as long as the results hash agrees, so the replica sends its endorsement upstream where it previously stayed silent. A round-change announcement that was signed for one round and then had its round number rewritten to a different one before delivery is accepted, instead of coming back refused with a partial-signature complaint.
